laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are strict. Long sentences apply for possessing illegal 'hard drugs'. Hard drugs include heroin, cocaine and synthetics.
laws.heading: Drug laws

laws.rule: A traditional bul (decree by traditional leadership) is in effect in Koror and Airai. This decree is a curfew in place between midnight and 5am in the hamlets (suburbs) to reduce petty crime related to drug use. A similar measure is in effect in the states of Ngarchelong and Ngiwal. Foreigners are unlikely to be the target of these measures and application is inconsistent. However, it is still recommended that you follow the advice of local authorities and have a genuine reason to be in these areas during these times. The legal drinking age is 21 years. visa-preparation.entry_summary: A visitor visa for up to 30 days is given on arrival. Submit the free online Palau Entry Form at most 72 hours before departure; it creates a QR code shown at check-in and on arrival. Bring an onward or return ticket and a passport with at least 6 months' validity.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: 30-day tourist visa on arrival, stamped within minutes.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Submit the Palau Entry Form at most 72 hours before departure (no charge; beware scam sites) and keep the QR code. Carry a passport valid at least 6 months, a return ticket and enough funds.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: 30 days, extendable twice by 30 days each; apply at least 7 days before expiry at the Division of Immigration (USD 50 each renewal).

steps.step: Submit the free Palau Entry Form at most 72 hours before departure and keep the QR code.
On arrival, show the passport (6 months' validity), return ticket and the QR code; the visa is stamped in.
To stay longer, apply at the Division of Immigration at least 7 days before the visa expires.
Arriving by private vessel: get an entry permit before arriving.

documents: Passport valid at least 6 months on entry
open_questions: Was the entry form submitted inside, not before, the 72-hour pre-departure window?
Is a meeting or conference visit drifting into employment, delivery or commercial operation?
Has Immigration and Labour answered the unpaid-speaking question in writing for this exact role?
Is a Digital Resident tourist extension being mistaken for physical work permission?
Does the local host have authority and time to obtain a labour permit before the event?
Will a technical fee, local business presence, FIAC or PGST registration create Palau tax obligations?
Have the relevant state, traditional leaders and community partners been included rather than treating national permission as the whole relationship?
Are books, equipment, merchandise and goods for sale assigned to a Palauan importer and customs process?
Is the 30-day visa on arrival free? The pages read name no charge for it.

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: A Palauan organisation should contact Immigration and the Bureau of Labour and Human Resources to obtain written classification and any labour permit before speaking, teaching, consulting, performing or operating a business.
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Submit the Palau Entry Form at most 72 hours before departure and retain its QR code. Carry a passport valid six months, onward ticket, funds, accommodation and a precise invitation for any business or conference purpose.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: The visitor or business visa is 30 days and can be extended twice for another 30 days each. Apply at least seven days before expiry; the published renewal fee is USD 50 each time.
baseline_unverified.from: Luke's earlier precursor notes; not verified against an official source and not an authority. Kept because no official page covers this point yet.

visa-preparation.recheck_note: Rechecked 2026-11-03: Smartraveller (updated 22 Jul 2026) confirms the 30-day visa on arrival and the free Palau Entry Form; the Bureau of Customs and Border Protection page confirms the two 30-day extensions at USD 50 and the criteria; the Palau Entry Form page confirms the 72-hour rule. Departure tax and environmental fee are in the airfare. No charge for the visa on arrival itself is named on the pages read.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Dress standards: Dress and behaviour standards are conservative. LGBTQIA+ information: Same-sex relationships are legal, but cultural attitudes can be conservative. Avoid public displays of affection. Every visitor must sign the Palau Pledge, which is stamped in the passport, to protect the environment and respect local traditions. Reef-toxic sunscreen is banned: customs may confiscate it, with fines of up to USD 100 per item.
